title: Expedited Exception Approvals and the Exigency Period: Recording Terms (Formulary Benefit)
content:
## Terms

Under the Formulary Benefit, when an expedited exception request is approved, the length of the exigency approval is worked out from the member's records.

An expedited approval's period is fixed only after the member has said whether they want an independent review of every earlier denial of the same drug.

An expedited approval is not recorded until every tier exception request of the member whose decision fell due earlier than the expedited request carries a decision on record.

An expedited approval is not recorded until every standard non-formulary exception request of the member whose decision fell due earlier than the expedited request carries a decision on record.

For the expedited queue a request falls due at its latest supporting statement plus the formulary's standard or expedited decision hours, according to the request's priority.

An expedited approval is effective on the decision date and runs for the exigency period, counted in calendar days with the decision date as day 1.

Read against the records, the two terms on when an expedited approval is recorded, taken with the definition of when a request falls due, mean the following. The member's exception history must show a decision for each of two kinds of earlier request: every tier exception request, and every standard non-formulary exception request, whose due moment (its latest supporting statement plus the decision hours of its own priority) comes before that of the expedited request. Until it does, the expedited approval is not recorded.

## Recording tool: `approve_expedited_exception_8cc2ac55`

**Capability.** One call adds one expedited approval decision to the request's case history, dated today, covering the drug at the tier given. The approval is effective today and runs the given number of calendar days, with today as day 1. Its expiration date is therefore today plus that number of days less one. The member's claims for the drug are covered at that tier through that date. The tool makes this single write. It checks nothing about eligibility, ordering or the values given.

**Invocation.** This is an agent-side tool. The agent unlocks `approve_expedited_exception_8cc2ac55` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `formulary_assignment_id` | reference number of the member's formulary assignment, as read from the formulary assignment lookup for the member | identifier |
| `source_exception_id` | reference number of the original exception request being approved, read from the member's exception history (the request row itself, not its statement row) | identifier |
| `drug_name` | the drug of the request | exactly one drug master list name: atorvastatin, lisinopril, metformin, sertraline, levothyroxine, sumatriptan, oxycodone-acetaminophen, insulin glargine-yfgn, Lantus, Eliquis, Xarelto, Jardiance, Ozempic, Mounjaro, Wegovy, Zepbound, Trelegy Ellipta, Breztri Aerosphere, Nurtec ODT, Ubrelvy, Humira, adalimumab-adaz, Dupixent, Skyrizi, Rinvoq, Enbrel, Biktarvy, Ibrance |
| `exception_type` | the kind of exception approved: `tier_exception` (a formulary drug covered at a lower cost-share tier) or `non_formulary_exception` (a drug coded non-formulary covered by exception) | enum |
| `approved_tier` | the cost-share tier at which the approved exception covers the drug | enum: `1` (the generic tier), `2` (the preferred brand tier), `3` (the non-preferred brand tier), `4` (the first specialty tier), `5` (the second specialty tier), `not_applicable` (only for a record that carries no approval; never correct on an approval) |
| `approval_days` | the length of the approval in calendar days, with today counted as day 1 | whole number of days, no decimals |

A parameter's presence means only that the value is needed at call time.

**Return.** The receipt carries:
- `formulary_exception_id`, the reference number of the approval decision;
- `source_exception_id`, the request approved;
- `drug_name`;
- `approved_tier`;
- `approval_effective_date`, today as YYYY-MM-DD;
- `approval_expiration_date`, the last day the approval is in force, as YYYY-MM-DD;
- status "approved".

Status "approved" means the approval was recorded. No other outcome is defined for this tool.

*Hypothetical date check.* An approval recorded on 10 May for 30 days runs from 10 May (day 1) through 8 June (day 30).
